version.changelog: v1.3.0: New feed strip workflow — dynamic vision prompt from JSON authors, anti-duplicate guard, updated output schema (feed_screenshot top-level). Resolves vision mismatch issue where model described wrong posts.

llm.summary: This skill does what it claims, but it uses a persistent Facebook login profile and an unsandboxed browser with weak URL and file cleanup safeguards, so it should be reviewed carefully before use.

dimensions.detail: A persistent authenticated browser profile and screenshots of group content are purpose-aligned, but they can contain sensitive session and private-group data. The artifact discloses where they are stored, but gives limited security, retention, and isolation guidance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses a local Python virtual environment and documented pip/Playwright installs, with no remote shell pipeline or suspicious custom package source. Dependencies are not pinned, so installs are not reproducible.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose browser automation, persistent login, screenshots, seen-post tracking, and optional cron use, but triggers such as monitor group and Facebook marketplace are broad and the runtime does not enforce the documented Facebook-only scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to the skill directory and user-selected screenshot paths, but it stores Facebook session state for weeks or months, keeps seen-post state, and deletes JPEG files from a user-controlled screenshot directory without confirming skill ownership.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose is coherent: it logs into Facebook, monitors group feeds, deduplicates posts, and saves screenshots for vision analysis. The concern is that the scrape command accepts any string beginning with http and then navigates a persistent, unsandboxed browser to it instead of enforcing a Facebook group URL.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable storing an authenticated Facebook browser session locally and saving screenshots of group content. Use a dedicated, private workspace, avoid shared screenshot folders, pass only real Facebook group URLs or IDs, and periodically delete .browser-data, .seen-posts.json, and screenshots when no longer needed. This should not be used on hosts where untrusted prompts or users can control the group URL or screenshot directory.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Persistent browser data, seen-post state, and screenshots are expected for this monitor, but the lack of an explicit permission boundary and retention guidance is a real review concern because the data may include authenticated session material and private content.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger phrases are not necessary for the stated Facebook-group monitoring task and could cause use in situations where the user did not clearly request authenticated scraping and screenshot capture.
[SQP-2] expected: Storing a persistent Facebook session and captured feed screenshots is central to the skill, but the artifacts understate the sensitivity of those local files and do not provide clear cleanup or protection instructions.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The hard-coded vi-VN locale and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh timezone are not a major security issue by themselves, but they are not explained as part of the skill's general Facebook monitoring purpose.
[T09] unexpected: The arbitrary-URL navigation and --no-sandbox browser launch are supported by the code and exceed the documented Facebook-group-only workflow, raising the impact of hostile or mistaken URLs.
[T09] unexpected: Screenshot cleanup is expected, but deleting every top-level .jpg in an arbitrary --shots-dir is broader than needed and could remove unrelated user images.
[T08] expected: Installing Playwright and related packages is expected, but the setup instructions do not pin versions or hashes, which weakens reproducibility rather than showing malicious dependency behavior.
